en: Pāṇini’s *Liṅgānuśāsana*: Now begins the section on feminine gender. 001 Gender.

002 Feminine nouns: 003 Those ending in the vowel ṛ—namely *mātṛ* (mother), *duhitṛ* (daughter), *svasṛ* (sister), *potṛ* (maternal uncle), and *nanāndṛ* (husband’s sister)—are feminine. 004 A verbal root (*dhātu*) ending in the suffix *anyu* is feminine; likewise, one ending in the suffix *pani* or *ū* is feminine.
005 *Aśani*, *bharaṇya*, and *araṇi* are masculine; 006 those ending in the suffix *min* are neuter; 007 *vahni*, *vṛṣṇi*, and *agni* are masculine.
008 The words *śroṇi*, *yoni*, and *ūrmi* [denote] both [masculine and feminine].
009 [Words ending in] the suffix *ktin*. 010 And those ending in long *ī*. Those ending in the suffix *pī*.

011. Feminine nouns ending in *ūṅ* and *āp*, as well as those ending in a primary suffix (*pratyaya*) with the marker *āp*. 012. A monosyllabic word ending in *y* or *v*, such as *pī* or those ending in *ū*. 013. The numerals beginning with *viṃśati* up to *ānavati*.
014 *Dundubhiḥ* [is used] for the axles;
015 *nābhiḥ* [is used] for a Kṣatriya;
016 both [are used] for other things in the masculine.
017 *talantaḥ*: A word ending in the suffix *tal* has the phonetic marker *ph*. 018 Words denoting earth, lightning, river, creeper, and woman [end in *tal*].
019 *yādas* is neuter.
020. *bhās*, *ruj*, *kruñc*, *diś*, *uṣṇih*, and *upānah* [are optionally feminine].
021. *sthūṇā* and *ūrṇā* [are optionally feminine] when used as neuter.
022. After *gṛha* and *śas*, [the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied] when the word is in the neuter gender.
023 *prāvṛṣ*, *vipruṣ*, *aṭṭi*, *tṛṭ*, *viṭ*, *tviṣ*.
024 *darvi*, *vidi*, *vedi*, *khani*, *śāni*, *aśri*, *veśi*, *kṛṣi*, *uṣadhi*, *kaṭa*, *aṅguli*: [the suffix] *ṅīp* is applied optionally.
025 *tithi*, *nāḍi*, *ruci*, *vīci*, *nāli*, *dhūli*, *kiki*, *kelicchavi*, *rātri*, etc., and *pāda*, etc.
026. *Śaṣkulī*, *rāji*, *kuṭaśani*, *varti*, *bhrukuṭi*, *truṭi*, *vali-paṅkti*;
027. *pratipad*, *āpad*, *vipat*, *sampat*, *śarad*, *saṃsad*, *pariṣad*, *uṣas*, *saṃvit*, *kṣut*, *punarmuk*, *samidh*;
028. *āśis*, *dhūḥ*, *pūr*, *gīr*, *dvār*.
029. *Apsumant*, *samās*, *sikatā*, and *varṣāṇām* are plural;
030. *ruāt*, *tvak*, *jyok*, *vāc*, *yavāgū*, *nau*, and *sphijaḥ*;
031. *tṛṭi*, *sīmā*, and *saṃbadhyāḥ*.
032 *cullī*, *veṇī*, and *khārī* [are feminine].
033 *tārā*, *dhārā*, *jyotsnā*, and so forth; as well as those ending in *-ā*. 034 *śalākā* is always feminine.
Thus ends the section on women.
Now begins the section on masculine nouns (pulliṅgādhikāra):
035. *Pumān* (masculine). 036. Words ending in *ghañ* and *ap*. [Note: *ghañ* and the suffix *ap* are used only in the sense of abstract action (*bhāvārtha*).]
037 And those ending in *ghañ*. Those ending in the suffix *ap* (i.e., *ac*).
038 Words denoting limbs of the body and words denoting fortune (*bhaga*) are neuter.
039 Those ending in *naṅ*. Those ending in the suffix *naṅ*.
040 *yācñā* (begging) is feminine. 041 A verbal root ending in *ky* is designated as *ghu*. [A word] ending in the suffix *kvi* is *ghu*. 042 *iṣudhiḥ* (quiver) is also feminine.
043 The words *deva*, *asura*, *ātman*, *svarga*, *giri*, *samudra*, *nakha*, *keśa*, *danta*, *stana*, *bhuja*, *kaṇṭha*, *khaḍga*, *śara*, and *paṅka* [are masculine].
044 The words *triviṣṭapa* and *tribhuvana* are neuter.
045 The word *dyauḥ* is feminine.
046. *iṣu* and *bāhu* are feminine; 047. *bāṇa* and *kāṇḍa* are also neuter; 048.
[Words] ending in *n* [are masculine].
049 The words *kratu*, *puruṣa*, *kapola*, *gulpha*, and *megha* [are masculine].
050 *Abhra* is neuter.
051 [The word *megha*] ends in the vowel *u*.
052. *Dhenu*, *rajju*, *kuhū*, *sarayu*, *tanu*, *reṇu*, and *priyaṅgu* are feminine.
053. In a compound, *rajju* may also be masculine.
054. *Śmaśru*, *jānu*, *vasu*, *svādu*, *aśru*, *jatu*, *trapu*, and *tālu* are neuter.
055. *vasu* is used in the sense of wealth (*artha*).
056. *madgu*, *madhu*, *sīdhu*, *śīdhu*, *sānu*, and *kamaṇḍalu* are also [masculine] in the neuter gender.
057. Those ending in *rut* (the letter *r*) [are masculine]; those ending in the suffix *pru* and *tu* [are also masculine].
058. *Dāru*, *kaśeru*, *jatu*, *vastu*, and *mastu* are neuter. 059. *Saktu* is also neuter. 060.
Words ending in *a* are neuter up to [the rule concerning] *raśmi*.
061. Words ending in the suffix *kopadh-* [are neuter].
062. The words *cibuka*, *śālūka*, *prātipadika*, *aṃśuka*, and *ulmuka* are neuter.

063. The words *kaṇṭaka*, *anīka*, *saraka*, *modaka*, *caṣaka*, *mastaka*, *pustaka*, *taḍāka*, *niṣka*, *śuṣka*, *varcaska*, *pināka*, *bhāṇḍaka*, *piṇḍaka*, *kaṭaka*, *śaṇḍaka*, *piṭaka*, *tālaka*, *phalaka*, and *pulāka* are neuter, and [may also be masculine].

064. [Words ending in] -ṭa and -pa [are neuter]. 065. *Kirīṭa*, *mukuṭa*, *lalāṭa*, *vaṭa*, *viṭa*, *śṛṅgāṭa*, *karāṭa*, and *loṣṭa* are neuter. 066. *Kuṭa*, *kūṭa*, *kapaṭa*, *kavāṭa*, *karpaṭa*, *naṭa*, *nikaṭa*, *kīṭa*, and *kaṭa* are [neuter] as well.
067. A word having *ṇ* as its penultimate letter [is neuter].
068. *Ṛṇa*, *lavaṇa*, *parṇa*, *toraṇa*, *raṇa*, and *uṣṇa* are neuter.
069. *Kārṣāpaṇa*, *svarṇa*, *suvarṇa*, *vraṇa*, *caraṇa*, *vṛṣaṇa*, *viṣāṇa*, *cūrṇa*, and *tṛṇa* are neuter, and [the last five] may also be masculine.
070. [Words ending in] -tha and -dha [are feminine]. 071. *kāṣṭha*, *pṛṣṭha*, *sriktha*, and *uktha* are neuter.
072. *Kāṣṭhā* is feminine when it means a direction.
073. *Tīrtha*, *protha*, *yūtha*, and *gāthā* are neuter.
074. A word having *n* as its penultimate letter [is neuter].
075. *Jaghana*, *ajina*, *tuhiṇa*, *kānana*, *vana*, *vṛjina*, *vipina*, *vetana*, *śāsana*, *sopāna*, *mithuna*, *śmaśāna*, *ratna*, *nimna*, and *cihna* are neuter.

076. The words *māna*, *yāna*, *abhidhāna*, *nalina*, *pulina*, *udyāna*, *śayana*, *āsana*, *sthāna*, *candana*, *ālāna*, *samāna*, *bhavana*, *vasana*, *saṃbhāvana*, *vibhāvana*, and *vimāna* are used in the neuter gender.
077. *Pauṣadha*. 078. The words *pāpa*, *rūpa*, *uḍupa*, *talpa*, *śilpa*, *puṣpa*, *śaṣpa*, *samīpa*, and *antarīpa* are used in the neuter gender.
079. *śūrpa*, *kutapa*, *kuṇapa*, *dvīpa*, and *viṭapa* are neuter. 080. A word ending in *bh* [and preceded by a vowel] is neuter. 081. *Talabha* is neuter.
082. *jṛmbha* is neuter. 083. A word having *m* as its penultimate letter [is neuter]. 084. *rukma*, *sidhma*, *yudhma*, *idhma*, *gulma*, *adhyātma*, and *kuṅkuma* are neuter.
085. *Saṃgrāma*, *dāḍima*, *kusuma*, *āśrama*, *kṣema*, *kṣauma*, and *homoddāma* are neuter; as well as [words ending in] -a. 086.
[Words] having *ya* as the penultimate letter [are neuter].
087. *Kisalaya*, *hṛdaya*, *indriya*, and *uttarīya* are neuter.
088. *gomaya*, *kaṣāya*, *malaya-anvaya*, and *avyaya* are neuter; and [the word] ending in *r* followed by *o* [is also neuter].
089. [The word] having *r* as its penultimate letter [is neuter].

090. Door-edges, expanses, buttermilk, crookedness, embankments, swift, small, heroes, shores, distant, hardship, openings, corners, pits, fearful, deep, cruel, variegated, armlets, the interior of a field, old age, bodies, caves, Mandāra trees, cages, unaging, bellies, courtyards, enmity, chowries, lotuses, abysses, hollows, huts, crabs, crossroads, Kashmir, waterless, cool, systems, machines, nobility, fields, friends, wives, paintings, urine, threads, faces, and eyes.

The words *gotra*, *aṅgulitra*, *bhalatra*, *śastra*, *śāstra*, *vastra*, *patra*, *pātra*, and *chatra* are neuter. The word *śukra* is neuter when it does not refer to a deity. The words *cakra*, *vajra*, *andhakāra*, *sāra*, *avāra*, *pāra*, *kṣīra*, *tomara*, *śṛṅgāra*, *bhṛṅgāra*, *mandāra*, *uśīra*, *timira*, and *śiśira* are both masculine and neuter.
093. [The following] have the letter *ṣ* as their penultimate (*ṣopadha*).
094. *śirīṣa*, *rjīṣa*, *ambarīṣa*, *pīyūṣa*, *purīṣa*, *kilbiṣa*, and *kalmāṣa* are neuter.
095. *yūṣa*, *karīṣa*, *miṣa*, *viṣa*, and *varṣa* are also neuter.
096. *Sopadha* [is masculine]. 097. *Panasa*, *bisa*, *busa*, and *sāhasa* are neuter.
098. *Camasa*, *aṃsa*, *rasa*, *niryāsa*, *upavāsa*, *kārpāsa*, *vāsa*, *bhāsa*, *kāsa*, *kāṃsa*, and *māṃsa* are both masculine and neuter.
099. The word *kaṃsa* [is used] for anything other than a living being. 100. Words denoting "rays" and "days. 101. *Dīdhitiḥ* is feminine.
102. *dināhana* is neuter. 103. Words denoting measures are [neuter]. 104. *droṇa* and *āḍhaka* are also neuter.
105. The word *mānika* is feminine when it denotes a measure of ten *khārīs*.
106. The words *dāra*, *akṣata*, *lāja*, and *sū* take the plural number. 107. Words ending in *nāḍī*, *jana*, and *upapada* [respectively] denote a wound, a limb, and a foot.
108. Marut, garut, tara, and ṛtvij; 109. Ṛṣi, rāśi, dṛti, granthi, krimi, dhvani, bali, kauli, mauli, ravi, kavi, kapi, and muni;
110. Dhvaja, gaja, muñja, and puñja.
111. *hasta*, *kuntānta*, *vrāta*, *vāta*, *dūta*, *dhūrta*, *sūta*, *cūta*, *muhūrta*;
112. *ṣaṇḍa*, *maṇḍa*, *karaṇḍa*, *bharaṇḍa*, *varaṇḍa*, *tuṇḍa*, *gaṇḍa*, *muṇḍa*, *pāṣaṇḍa*, *śikhaṇḍa*;
113. *vaṃśa*, *aṃśa*, *puroḍāśa*.
114. Indeed, here are the words *kanda*, *kunda*, and *budbuda*.
115. [Words ending in] *argha*, *pathin*, *mathin*, *ṛbhukṣin*, *stamba*, *nitamba*, and *pūga*.
116. [Words ending in] *pallava*, *palvala*, *kapha*, *repha*, *śepha*, *kaṭāha*, *nirvyūha*, *maṭha*, *maṇi*, *taraṅga*, *turaṅga*, *gandha*, *skandha*, *mṛdaṅga*, *saṅga*, *samudra*, and *puṅkha*.
117. *Sārathi*, *atithi*, *kukṣi*, *vasti*, *pāṇi*, and *añjali*. Thus ends the section on masculine nouns; now begins the section on neuter nouns.
118. [A word ending in] the neuter gender [is called *napuṃsaka*].

119. A word ending in the suffix *lyuṭ* [denotes] the abstract state (*bhāva*). 120. And a word ending in a *niṣṭhā* suffix [also denotes the abstract state]. *Niṣṭhā* [refers to] the past passive participles.
121. [The suffixes] *tva* and *ṣyañ* are *taddhita* [suffixes]. That which ends in the suffixes *tva* or *ṣyañ* [is called a *bhāva-rūpa* noun].
122. And [the suffix *tva* is applied] after words denoting qualities (*guṇavacana*) beginning with *brāhmaṇa*, when [the sense of] "action" (*karman*) is expressed.
123. The suffixes *ya*, *ḍhak*, *yak*, *añ*, *aṇ*, *vuñ*, and *cha* are applied to form nouns denoting the state (*bhāva*) or the object (*karman*).
[These include those ending in] *pyat*, *ya*, *ḍhak*, *yak*, *añ*, *aṇ*, *vuñ*, and *cha*. 124. The *avyayībhāva* compound.
125. Singularity for a copulative compound (dvandva).
126. In the case of non-linguistic usage, [the term *chāyā*] is used for the winter and cool seasons, as well as for day and night.
127. A *tatpuruṣa* compound that is not a *nañ*-compound nor a *karmadhāraya* [is neuter]. 128. [The term *chāyā* is used] in the sense of "not small" (abundant).
129. *Rāja*, *manuṣya*, and *pūrva* [form masculine nouns]. 130. *Surā*, *senā*, *chāyā*, *śālā*, and *niśā* [are feminine], as is *strī*.
131. The remaining [compounds] follow the gender of the final member. 132. The words *rātra*, *ahna*, and *aha* are masculine.
133. [The words] *apatha*, *puṇyāha*, and *napuṃsaka* [are neuter]. 134. A word ending in *rātri* preceded by a numeral [is feminine]. 135. A *dvigu* compound [ending in *rātri*] is also [feminine].
136. *iṣu-sant-*: [the word] ending with the suffix *u* preceded by *iṣu*. 137. *arciḥ* is feminine.
138. *chadiḥ* is exclusively feminine.
139. The terms *mukha*, *nayana*, *loha*, *vana*, *māṃsa*, *rudhira*, *kārmuka*, *vivara*, *jala*, *hala*, *dhana*, and *anna* [are masculine].
140. [The synonyms] *sīra*, *artha*, and *odana* are masculine. 141. *Vaktra*, *netra*, *araṇya*, and *gāṇḍīva* are also masculine.
142. *Aṭavī* (forest) is feminine. 143. A word having *l* as its penultimate letter [is feminine]. 144. *Tūla*, *upala*, *tāla*, *kusūla*, *tarala*, *kambala*, *devala*, and *vṛṣala* are masculine.

145. *Śīla*, *mūla*, *maṅgala*, *sāla*, *kamala*, *tala*, *musala*, *kuṇḍala*, *palala*, *mṛṇāla*, *vāla*, *nigala*, *palāla*, *biḍāla*, *khila*, and *śūla* are [masculine]; they are also [neuter] in the masculine. 146. Numbers beginning with "hundred" (*śata*) are [feminine]. 147. *Śata*, *ayuta*, and *prayuta* are [feminine]; they are also [masculine].
148. *Lakṣā* and *koṭi* are feminine; 149. *śaṅku* is masculine;
150. *saharuā* occurs in some instances.
151. A word ending in the suffix *man* is neuter when it does not denote an agent (*akartari*). 152. The word *brāhmaṇ* is masculine as well [as neuter].
153. The words *nāman* and *roman* are neuter.
154. A word ending in the suffix *as* (the present participle) is neuter when it consists of two syllables. 155. *Apsaras* is feminine. 156. A word ending in *trā* [is feminine].
157. *Yātrā*, *mātrā*, *bhastrā*, *daṃṣṭrā*, and *varatrā* are exclusively feminine.
158. *Bhṛtrā*, *amitra*, *chātra*, *putra*, *mantra*, *vṛtra*, *meḍhra*, and *uṣṭra* are masculine.
159. *Patra*, *pātra*, *pavitra*, *sūtra*, and *chatra* are both masculine and neuter.

160. *Bala*, *kusuma*, *śulba*, *pattana*, and *raṇa* are [names for various things]. 161. *Padma*, *kamala*, and *utpala* are masculine as well [as neuter]. 162. *Āhava* and *saṃgrāma* are masculine.
163. *Āji* is used only in the feminine. 164. [Words denoting] the genus of fruit [are feminine]. 165. [Words denoting] the genus of trees are used only in the feminine.
166. *viyat*, *jagat*, *sakṛt*, *śakan*, *pṛṣat*, *śakṛt*, *yakṛt*, *udaśvit*;
167. *navanīta*, *avatāna*, *anṛta*, *amṛta*, *nimitta*, *vitta*, *citta*, *pitta*, *vrata*, *rajata*, *vṛtta*, *palita*;
168. *śrāddha*, *kuliśa*, *daiva*, *pīṭha*, *kuṇḍa*, *bhāṇḍa*, *aṅka*, *aṅgada*, *dadhi*, *sakthi*, *akṣi*, *āsya*, *āspada*, *ākāśa*, *kaṇva*, *bīja*.

169. *daiva* is also [neuter] when referring to a man. 170. *dhānya*, *ājya*, *sasya*, *rūpya*, *kupya*, *paṇya*, *vaṇrya*, *dhiṣṇya*, *havya*, *kavya*, *kāvya*, *satya*, *apatya*, *amūlya*, *śikya*, *kuḍa*, *madya*, *hamrya*, *tūrya*, and *sainya* are neuter. 171. *dvandva*, *barha*, *duḥkha*, *baḍiśa*, *piccha*, *bimba*, *kuṭumba*, *kavaca*, *vara*, *śara*, and *vṛndāraka* are neuter.
172. *Akṣa* means a sense faculty (*indriya*). Thus ends the section on neuter nouns.
Now begins the section on women and men (strīpuṃsādhikāra). [The following are examples:
173. Woman and man; 174. Cow, jewel, staff, fist, pāṭali, bladder, silk-cotton tree, trutī, ink, and ray.

175. *mṛtyu*, *sīdhu*, *karkandhu*, *kiṣku*, *kaṇḍu*, and *reṇu* [are neuter]. 176. A word denoting a quality ending in *u* is also neuter. 177. [A word] expressing the sense of "offspring" in a secondary derivative (*taddhita*) [is neuter].
Thus ends the section on women and men.
Now begins the section on masculines and neuters (puṃnapuṃsakādhikāra).

178. [The following words] are both masculine and neuter: 179. *ghṛta* (clarified butter), *bhūta* (a being), *musta* (nardus grass), *kṣvelita* (playful movement), *airāvata* (the elephant Airāvata), *pustaka* (book), *busta* (a heap), and *lohita* (red).
180. [Words ending in] *śṛṅga*, *argha*, *nidāgha*, *udyama*, *śalya*, and *dṛḍha* [are masculine].
181. [Words ending in] *vraja*, *kuñja*, *kutha*, *kūrca*, *prastha*, *darpa*, *arbha*, *ardharca*, *darbha*, and *puccha* [are masculine].
182. [Words ending in] *kabandha*, *oṣadhi*, and *āyudha* [are masculine].
183. Daṇḍa, maṇḍa, khaṇḍa, śava, saindhava, pārśva, ākāśa, kuśa, kīśa, aṅkuśa, and kuliśa;
184. Gṛha, meha, deha, paṭṭa, paṭaha, aṣṭāpada, ambuda, and kakuda.
Thus ends the section on masculine and neuter nouns.
185. The remaining [words] are *liṅga* (grammatical gender). 186. The indeclinables (*avyaya*) are *kati*, *yuṣmad*, and *asmad*.
187. A numeral ending in *ṣ* or *n* is feminine (*strī*). (The remainder follows the subsequent [word]).
188. And [words] expressing qualities [are used in the same way].
189. So too [words ending in] kṛtya suffixes.
190. The suffix *yuṭ* is also applied after verbal roots to denote the instrument (*karaṇa*) and the locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
191. The words beginning with *sarva* are called pronouns (*sarvanāman*).
Thus ends the instruction on gender.
